identity_notes: This identity's label spellings ('Olive Leaf Extract', 'Oleuropein', 'Tyrosol', 'Hydroxytyrosol/Tyrosol', 'Verbascoside/Oleuropein', 'Benolea') cover both whole olive leaf extract products and isolated marker compounds (oleuropein, hydroxytyrosol, tyrosol). A very large share of the retrieved literature instead studies these same marker compounds sourced from OLIVE OIL or WINE (measuring endogenous formation/bioavailability from those different product categories) -- these were rejected as different_substance since they do not concern the leaf-extract or isolated-supplement label material; reviewers should treat this as a judgment call given the compounds are chemically identical, and reconsider if the curator wants oil/wine-sourced PK data folded in as supporting mechanism evidence. Among kept olive-LEAF-specific records, the best-supported, most consistent EXACT-MATCH efficacy signal is for BLOOD PRESSURE in hypertensive/prehypertensive adults, with a large multicenter RCT (40990594, n=621) and multiple concordant meta-analyses (33868820, 36271405, 40325976, 42303499) generally finding benefit that is more pronounced at doses >=500-1000 mg/day. Glycemic-control evidence is mixed-to-null in most single-agent trials and the two most recent meta-analyses (38287654, 41848522) reach different conclusions on glucose/lipid outcomes depending on trial-quality stratification. A meaningful fraction of positive records are combination products (olive leaf + green coffee/beetroot, + citrus flavonoids, + potassium, + fenugreek/bergamot, + monacolin K/CoQ10/grape seed) or non-oral routes (topical creams for herpes labialis, a mouth rinse for chemotherapy-induced mucositis) and were flagged related_form_differs/route caveats accordingly. One retracted publication (36875283, an in silico COVID-19 docking study) was excluded entirely as off_topic. No serious human safety signals (hepatotoxicity, organ injury) were identified in this retrieved scope, in contrast to several other botanicals in this partition.
